user_pushback_at_walk_time.trigger: User read upstream docs at https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/main/docs/commands.md and quoted /opsx:sync as 'Optional command. Merge delta specs from a change into main specs. Archive will prompt to sync if needed, so you typically don't need to run this manually.' — NOT deprecated.
user_pushback_at_walk_time.verification: Verified via openspec --help (no 'sync' CLI command — only 'archive' which auto-syncs) AND inspection of .claude/commands/opsx/sync.md (no deprecation language; frontmatter category Workflow, tags include experimental but not deprecated). Original 'deprecated' claim originated in issue #6's body, propagated through D7 + EW1 + spec language without verification.
user_pushback_at_walk_time.principle_captured: User stated: 'we want to fully and cleanly support the openspect functionality set at 1.3.1 unless there is a real reason not to. i don't think we need to write requirements around it.' Saved as project memory `orbit-supports-full-openspec-1-3-1`.

pushback_verification: All 4 review findings verified at walk-time. TR1 verified — task 3.4 has no 'sandbox' definition. TR2 verified — dependency lives in skill prose only. TR3 verified — Workflow-tool framing scenario lacks negative test. TR4 verified — Try-it nudge requires real project idea. PLUS at walk-time the user's pushback on the propagated 'deprecated upstream' claim about /opsx:sync was verified — EW1 reversal added to this walk.

resolutions.action: Defined 'fresh sandbox' inline in task 3.4: clean temp directory (e.g., `mktemp -d`) + same Node version as project's package.json engines field (or current LTS if unspecified) + `openspec init --tools claude` from clean state + documented overlay copy + documented prune step + `openspec --version` confirming match. Closes FF4's 'if possible' escape hatch by giving implementing AI concrete steps.

Per user 'i don't think we need to write requirements around it'. Under project memory `orbit-supports-full-openspec-1-3-1`, orbit's continued use of the upstream openspec-sync-specs primitive is implicit and doesn't warrant a normative spec requirement. Dependency continues to live in `.claude/skills/openspec-archive-change/SKILL.md:65` prose. Captured rationale in design.md item 9.

Added negative-test scenario to orbit-onboard Identity statement section: 'Framing MUST NOT use augmentation language' — enumerates forbidden phrases (augments cleanly, overlay on top of, layered on top of, extends upstream, additive to upstream — case-insensitive). Negative test more useful than positive prescription.

Split Try-it nudge section requirement's Closing recommendation scenario into 2: (a) named-mode for concrete project ideas; (b) bare-mode for orientation-only users (collaborators new to orbit, AI sessions getting cold context, users without concrete ideas yet). Preserves no-demo-change discipline while surfacing bare-mode explore as the no-decision-yet entry point per orbit-explore conventions.

REVERSED EW1 (from address-reviews iter-2) which was based on propagated false 'deprecated upstream' claim. Actions: (a) Removed task 1.2 (delete sync.md command); (b) Removed sync.md from task 3.6 README rm-step documentation (only feedback prune now); (c) Removed sync.md absence-verification from tasks 5.3a, 5.4a; (d) Updated task 5.5a to confirm sync IS in the Quick-reference table (not excluded); (e) Removed `(currently: sync.md)` reference from orbit-onboard Verification failures distinguish scenario; (f) Removed sync.md from orbit-onboard Verify pruned upstream files are absent scenario; (g) Removed `(e.g., opsx/sync.md)` reference from orbit-onboard Quick-reference All current /opsx:* commands listed scenario; (h) Recategorized opsx/sync.md from 'not shipped' to 'orbit-modified' in orbit-conventions Overlay file disposition Commands follow same 4-category framework scenario; (i) Simplified orbit-conventions Internal-run JSON summary format sync_specs parenthetical — dropped 'retained under pegging strategy' framing, just describes the field; (j) Simplified orbit-run-summary-emit Emit scope /opsx:sync-specs bullet — dropped 'primitive only under pegging strategy ... user-callable command pruned' framing, just describes invocation pattern; (k) Updated design.md item 6 to drop sync.md from rm-step description; (l) Added design.md item 7 documenting the EW1-reversal rationale and lesson learned. Resulting state: /opsx:sync retained as user-callable command; openspec-sync-specs SKILL retained as primitive; orbit's archive still uses it via subagent.

resolutions.anchor_break_observation_meta: Iter-4 caught the propagated 'deprecated upstream' false claim — by the user, not by review. 4 prior review cycles all anchored on the false premise: in-context iter-1 didn't question it, external Codex iter-1 didn't question it (Codex only flagged the language stale-spread to other specs, not the underlying claim), fresh-context Claude iter-2 didn't question it, in-context --thorough iter-3 didn't question it. The user catching it by reading upstream docs directly is the kind of pushback discipline that no review mode catches automatically. Lesson: verify deprecation claims against current upstream state, don't trust prior summaries (now captured in project memory).
